subject: History
title: Ancient Rome Quiz
sourceSummary: Key people, places, and ideas from the Roman Republic and Empire.

questions.prompt: According to legend, who founded the city of Rome?
questions.opener: The legend involves twin brothers raised by a wolf. One of them ended up with the city named after him.
questions.explanation: Legend says the twins Romulus and Remus founded Rome in 753 BCE, and Romulus became its first king.

questions.prompt: What was the Senate in the Roman Republic?
questions.opener: Rome had no single ruler during the Republic. So who actually decided things?
choices: A council of leading citizens that advised on laws and policy
questions.explanation: The Senate was a body of experienced statesmen (mostly patricians) that guided Roman policy, finances, and foreign affairs.

questions.prompt: Name one way the Romans made travel and trade across their empire easier, and briefly say why it helped.
questions.answer: They built a huge network of straight, paved roads (and also aqueducts, bridges, and safe sea routes). Good roads let armies, messengers, and merchants move quickly and reliably in almost any weather.
questions.rubric: Full credit: names a specific infrastructure (roads/bridges/aqueducts/ports) AND explains the benefit. Partial: names it without the benefit.

questions.prompt: Who was the first Roman emperor?
questions.opener: Careful — the most famous Roman name here was never actually an emperor. Think about who came just after him.
questions.explanation: Octavian took the name Augustus and became the first emperor in 27 BCE, ending the Republic.

questions.prompt: In a sentence, explain what 'Pax Romana' means and why it mattered.
questions.opener: 'Pax' is the Latin root of a word you already know in English. Start by translating the phrase.
questions.answer: 'Pax Romana' means 'Roman Peace' — roughly 200 years (27 BCE–180 CE) of relative stability across the empire, which allowed trade, building, and culture to flourish.
questions.rubric: Full credit: translates the term AND notes it was a long period of stability that helped trade/culture. Partial: only the translation.
